name: What is the difference between an open-concept kitchen and a semi-open kitchen?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an open-concept kitchen and a semi-open kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: An open-concept kitchen fully integrates with adjacent living areas, typically by removing walls entirely to create one large, continuous space. A semi-open kitchen, however, maintains some degree of separation, perhaps through a large archway, half-wall, or a significant opening that provides connectivity without complete integration. Semi-open designs offer more defined zones while still promoting interaction and light flow, serving as a middle ground between traditional and fully open layouts.
acceptedAnswer.description: An open-concept kitchen fully integrates with living areas, while a semi-open kitchen provides partial separation, offering a middle ground between open and traditional layouts.
